<!--more-->

Yeah, I know. It's pretty obvious which countries contribute most to euro area GDP growth: the larger economies. But let's do this exercise anyways. We will use the `eurostat` package to obtain data from Eurostat and calculate a euro area member state's contribution to overall euro area GDP growth.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(eurostat)
library(ggplot2)
library(zoo)
```

### Data

The `eurostat` package comes with a list of euro area countries. This is very useful when you only want to download data for euro area countries.

```{r}
ctr <- "AT"
```


### Sectoral breakdown of employment


```{r, message = FALSE}
emp <- get_eurostat(id = "namq_10_a10_e", cache = FALSE,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

valueadded <- get_eurostat(id = "namq_10_a10", cache = FALSE,
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```


```{r, fig.height=3.5,  fig.show = "hold", out.width = "50%"}
temp <- emp %>%
  filter(na_item == "EMP_DC",
         nace_r2 != "TOTAL",
         unit %in% c("PC_TOT_PER", "PC_TOT_HW", "PC_TOT_JOB"),
         geo == ctr) %>%
  group_by(na_item) %>%
  filter(time == max(time)) %>%
  ungroup()

temp_order <- temp %>%
  group_by(nace_r2) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(values)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(value))
temp_order <- temp_order$nace_r2

temp <- temp %>%
  mutate(nace_r2 = factor(nace_r2, levels = temp_order))

ggplot(temp, aes(x = nace_r2, y = values, fill = unit)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge")


temp <- valueadded %>%
  filter(geo == ctr,
         s_adj == "SCA",
         nace_r2 != "TOTAL",
         na_item == "B1G",
         unit == "PC_TOT",
         time %in% as.Date(c("2017-10-01", "2018-10-01", "2019-10-01"))) %>%
  mutate(time = as.yearqtr(time),
         time = as.character(time))

temp_order <- temp %>%
  group_by(nace_r2) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(values)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(value))
temp_order <- temp_order$nace_r2

temp <- temp %>%
  mutate(nace_r2 = factor(nace_r2, levels = temp_order))

ggplot(temp, aes(x = nace_r2, y = values, fill = time)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge")
```

## Unemployment

```{r}
unemp <- get_eurostat(id = "une_rt_m",
                      filters = list(s_adj = c("NSA", "SA"),
                                     geo = ctr),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(values)) # Drop NAs
```

### Unemployment by age group

```{r, fig.height=3.5,  fig.show = "hold", out.width = "50%"}
temp <- unemp %>%
  filter(s_adj == "NSA",
         sex == "T",
         age %in% c("Y25-74", "Y_LT25"),
         unit == "THS_PER",
         time >= "2019-01-01")

ggplot(temp, aes(x = time, y = values, fill = age)) +
  geom_col()

temp <- unemp %>%
  filter(s_adj == "NSA",
         sex == "T",
         unit == "PC_ACT",
         time >= "2019-01-01")

ggplot(temp, aes(x = time, y = values, colour = age)) +
  geom_line()

```

### Unemployment by sex

```{r, fig.height=3.5,  fig.show = "hold", out.width = "50%"}
temp <- unemp %>%
  filter(s_adj == "NSA",
         sex != "T",
         age == "TOTAL",
         unit == "THS_PER",
         time >= "2019-01-01")

ggplot(temp, aes(x = time, y = values, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge")

temp <- unemp %>%
  filter(s_adj == "NSA",
         sex != "T",
         age == "TOTAL",
         unit == "PC_ACT",
         time >= "2019-01-01")

ggplot(temp, aes(x = time, y = values, colour = sex)) +
  geom_line()

```
